title: Kalimpong's offbeat villages compared: Lava, Rishop, Lolegaon, Sillery
summary: Choose Rishop for the widest Kanchenjunga sunrise, Lava for Neora Valley and the monastery, Lolegaon for old forest and the canopy walk, and Sillery Gaon for the Teesta view and Lepcha history. Most travellers pair two villages with one or two nights in Kalimpong town.
meta_description: Lava, Rishop, Lolegaon or Sillery Gaon? Compare altitude, views, distance from Kalimpong, costs and best months to pick the right Kalimpong village.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Kalimpong district has four villages that most travellers choose between: Lava, Rishop, Lolegaon and Sillery Gaon. All are quiet, all run mainly on family homestays, and all can show you Kanchenjunga on a clear morning. They differ in height, in what you do there and in how easy they are to reach.

If you want one rule: pick Rishop for the mountain view, Lava for forest and wildlife, Lolegaon for a gentle forest stay with children, and Sillery Gaon for a short trip from Kalimpong with a dose of history. Lava and Rishop sit close together and pair naturally. Lolegaon fits on the way to Lava. Sillery Gaon lies in another direction, towards Pedong and the Sikkim border, and suits a short trip or a route on to the Old Silk Route.
Below we compare them side by side, then look at each in turn, and finish with sample combinations and practical advice on roads, money and seasons.

sections.heading: Side by side
paras: The table gives approximate figures. Distances are by the usual road from Kalimpong town, and homestay rates are indicative per person per night including meals for 2025–26. Rates rise in October and during school holidays, and fall a little in the quieter months.

sections.heading: Lava: forest, monastery and Neora Valley
paras: Lava is the largest of the four, with a small bazaar, a big Karma Kagyu monastery opened in 1990 and a forest lodge run by the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation. Its main draw is Neora Valley National Park, which is entered with a permit and a guide arranged in Lava. The park is closed from about mid-June to mid-September.

Lava is cooler than Kalimpong and often wrapped in mist by early afternoon, so plan sightseeing for the morning. Mountain views are partial from the village itself; for the full panorama you go up to Rishop or out to Kolakham. Choose Lava if you care about birds, forest walks and a slightly more lively village with shops and transport. It is also on a road down to Gorubathan and the Dooars, which helps when NH10 is closed by landslides.

sections.heading: Rishop: the widest mountain view
paras: Rishop, also spelt Rishyap, sits on a ridge at about 2,590 m, the highest of the four. It has no bazaar, only homestays and cottages spread along the ridge. From Tiffin Dara, a short climb above the village, the snow peaks of Sikkim stretch across the northern horizon, with Kanchenjunga at the centre. On a clear morning between October and February it is the best sunrise view in the district.

Rishop is cold. Nights from December to February drop below freezing, and light snow is possible some winters. It suits travellers who want quiet, photography and short walks, including the 4 km forest trail to Lava. Choose Rishop if the mountain view is the point of your trip, and pair it with a night in Lava.

sections.heading: Lolegaon: old forest and an easy pace
paras: Lolegaon is a Lepcha village at about 1,675 m, at the end of a ridge among tall oak, cypress and cryptomeria. Its heritage forest has a canopy walk that children love, and the sunrise point at Jhandi Dara, a ridge of prayer flags about 4–5 km away, faces the Kanchenjunga range. Kafer, close by, has an open view in the evening.

It is the furthest of the four from Kalimpong, about 55 km and 2–2.5 hours, and public transport is thin: one or two shared jeeps a day. It is lower and milder than Lava and Rishop, which makes it more comfortable in winter. Choose Lolegaon for a gentle forest stay, especially with children, and add it before Lava on a longer circuit.

sections.heading: Sillery Gaon: the Teesta and Lepcha history
paras: Sillery Gaon is a small homestay village at about 1,830 m above Pedong, roughly 30 km from Kalimpong. Many rooms face Kanchenjunga, and a walk of about 3 km leads to Ramitey Dara, where the Teesta winds through the valley in a long run of bends far below. The slopes still carry cinchona planted in British times.

History runs close here. Pedong's Sangchen Dorjee monastery dates from Bhutanese rule, and the ruins of Damsang Fort, linked to the Lepcha king Gaeboo Achyuk, stand nearby; Lepchas gather there every 20 December. The old trade route to Tibet over Jelep La ran this way. Choose Sillery Gaon for a short trip from Kalimpong or as a stepping stone to Aritar, Zuluk or Gangtok. The last stretch of road from Pedong is steep and narrow.

sections.heading: Sample combinations
paras: Most trips combine one or two villages with Kalimpong town. These are the patterns that work best on the ground, given the roads and the way the villages sit.
list: Three nights: Kalimpong two nights, Sillery Gaon one night. Short drives and a good mix of town and village.
Four nights: Kalimpong one night, Lava one night, Rishop two nights. Two chances at the Rishop sunrise.
Five nights: Kalimpong two nights, Lava two nights with a Neora Valley day, Rishop one night.
Six nights: Kalimpong two nights, Lolegaon one, Lava one, Rishop one, Sillery Gaon one, then down to the plains or on to Sikkim.
With Sikkim: end at Sillery Gaon and cross via Rhenock to Gangtok, Aritar or Zuluk. Foreigners need Sikkim permits. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Roads, money and seasons
paras: Hill roads here average 25–35 km an hour, so do not plan more than one village change a day. Shared jeeps link Kalimpong with Lava, Pedong and, less often, Lolegaon, but there is no shared transport to Rishop and only local jeeps to Sillery Gaon. A reserved car for a village transfer costs about ₹1,500–3,200 depending on distance, indicative.

Carry cash. Lava has limited ATMs that can run dry, Pedong has few and Rishop, Lolegaon and Sillery Gaon have none. Mobile signal is patchy in all four, and power cuts happen in bad weather, so bring a torch and a power bank.

October and November are the best months for views. December to February is clear but cold, especially in Rishop and Lava. March to May brings rhododendrons and birds, with haze after mid-morning. From June to September, landslides close NH10 and the village roads, Neora Valley is shut and views are rare. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which Kalimpong village has the best Kanchenjunga view?
faqs.a: Rishop, from the Tiffin Dara viewpoint above the village, gives the widest view of the range, thanks to its height of about 2,590 m. Sillery Gaon and Lolegaon's Jhandi Dara also have good views. Lava's own view is partial. All depend on weather; October to February at sunrise gives the best odds.

faqs.q: Lava or Rishop: which should I choose?
faqs.a: Do both if you can; they are only 11 km apart by road. If you must choose, pick Rishop for the mountain view and quiet, and Lava for Neora Valley, the monastery, birds and easier transport. Lava also has a forest lodge and a small bazaar, while Rishop has only homestays.

faqs.q: Which village is best with children?
faqs.a: Lolegaon, for the canopy walk, gentle forest paths and milder nights at about 1,675 m. Sillery Gaon also suits families, though the road up is steep. Rishop and Lava are fine for older children who cope with cold. Carry snacks and basic medicines, since shops in the villages are few.

faqs.q: Which village is easiest to reach from Siliguri?
faqs.a: Sillery Gaon and Lava are the easiest, at about 3.5–4 hours by car. Lava also has its own road via Gorubathan, useful when NH10 is closed. Lolegaon and Rishop take a little longer, about 4–4.5 hours. Shared jeeps go to Kalimpong, then onward jeeps to Lava and Pedong.

faqs.q: How many villages can I fit in a week?
faqs.a: Three or four comfortably, with one or two nights in Kalimpong. Change villages no more than once a day and give each at least one full night, since sunrise is often the main reason to be there. Moving every night is possible but tiring on slow hill roads.

faqs.q: Are homestays in these villages comfortable?
faqs.a: They are simple but generally clean, with attached bathrooms in most rooms, thick quilts and home-cooked meals. Hot water may come by geyser or bucket, and heaters are not always available. Standards vary by house, so ask for recent photos and confirm what is included before paying an advance.

faqs.q: Can I visit the villages in the monsoon?
faqs.a: It is possible but rarely rewarding. From June to September roads are slippery and landslides common, Neora Valley is closed and the mountains are usually in cloud. If you travel then, keep a spare day, travel in daylight and use Lava's Gorubathan road if NH10 is blocked. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Do I need permits for these villages?
faqs.a: No. Lava, Rishop, Lolegaon and Sillery Gaon are all in Kalimpong district and need no permits for Indians or foreigners. Neora Valley National Park needs an entry permit and guide. Continuing into Sikkim needs an Inner Line Permit for foreigners, and Zuluk needs a protected area permit.

faqs.q: How much should I budget per day in the villages?
faqs.a: Homestays with all meals cost about ₹1,200–2,200 per person per night, indicative. Add transport: ₹100–150 for a shared jeep seat or ₹1,500–3,200 for a reserved car between villages. Sunrise cars cost ₹600–1,200. Guides cost ₹300–1,000. Budget travellers can manage on about ₹2,000–2,600 a day.
